title: Heterogeneous execution adapter with runtime quant telemetry and safety sentinel
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight runtime adapter that can make per-request kernel routing decisions across FP16, FP8, and INT8 execution paths using precomputed quantization profiles and live telemetry. The adapter ("heterogeneous execution adapter") serves as a concise decision layer between the request router and the kernel executor. It must ensure accuracy guardrails via shadow calibration checks, attach traceable telemetry tags to each decision, and be latency-budget aware so high-SLO traffic prefers safer, lower-latency paths. This ticket covers design and implementation of the adapter, the minimal calibration shadow-run flow for conservative acceptance gating, and integration points for telemetry-driven policy updates.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter exposes a single decision API used by serving runtime to select kernel path: returns {path: one of FP16|FP8|INT8, reason_code, telemetry_tags}
Per-request decision includes a confidence score derived from quantization profile metrics and recent calibration deltas
Shadow calibration: at least 5% of sampled requests are executed on candidate path in parallel (no external effect) and results are compared for accuracy drift within tolerances
Adapter attaches telemetry tags (profile_id, path_selected, profile_version, confidence_score, calibration_sample) to tracing spans and metrics emitted to observability stack
Latency budget policy: requests with remaining_time < threshold are routed to conservative FP16 path regardless of confidence when risk > configured threshold
Integration tests validating kernel selection logic across synthetic distributions for sequence length, batch size, and prefix reuse
Performance overhead of adapter decision < 0.5 ms p50 and < 2 ms p99 in production-like environment
implementation_notes: Design a compact decision vector combining: quant_profile.score (expected token-level AUC loss), per-layer sensitivity score, recent drift metric (EWMA of shadow delta), and request meta (seq_len, batch_size, latency_budget)
Implement a deterministic scoring function so decisions are reproducible for a given profile_version + input hash; store scoring hyperparams in configmap to enable hot updates

Shadow calibration flow: instrument the executor to fork a best-effort async execution against candidate kernel (no affect on response) and compute lightweight metric (token-level topk overlap and perplexity delta) then report back to adapter
Safety sentinel: add a hard override table for models and routes marked high-risk (PII-sensitive customers) that force FP16/FP32; respect customer-level policy from RBAC config
Telemetry: emit metrics per decision: adapter.decisions.count{path}, adapter.confidence.histogram, adapter.shadow.delta.histogram, adapter.overrides.count; and add trace tags for span linking

Config knobs: sample_rate for shadow runs, confidence_thresholds per model family, latency_budget_thresholds, and drift_alert_window; expose via runtime flags and Console feature flags for gradual rollout
Fallbacks: if adapter cannot reach profile store or calibration service, default to most conservative path and emit an incident metric
Ensure the adapter is language-agnostic: provide a small C++ runtime library and a thin Rust binding to integrate into executor core
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring function determinism and edge cases (zero-length sequence, extremely large batch)
Integration tests with mocked executor: validate decision mapping across FP16/FP8/INT8 when profiles indicate different expected losses
Synthetic workload e2e: run three traffic patterns (chat-like short requests, long-completion inference, high-batch embedding-like) and verify path distributions match policy targets
Shadow calibration accuracy suite: compare top-1/3 token overlap and normalized perplexity delta across sampled requests; assert drift within configured tolerance over 10k samples
Performance regression: measure adapter p50/p99 in CI against baseline and gate on regressions >20%
Safety verification: simulate profile store outage and confirm all requests route to conservative path and an alert is fired
Chaos test: introduce delayed calibration returns and ensure timeout handling does not block live responses
